name: assembly-newsh2-279
summary: A ground machine set into a rock wall (three 2x2 pieces in a row: newsh2-279, -281, -283). Three thick purple octagonal armour caps along the middle, a short connector block between each pair of caps, and a row of upright purple canisters (hard-edged tanks running down-screen) under and between the caps. Grey boulders with beige stones surround it along the top edge and at the lower-left and lower-right. Shape language: hard, chamfered purple metal plates stacked in tiers (caps highest, canisters below, connectors between), matte round boulders around them.

concept.use: design guide; the sprite decides outline, proportions and colours

traits: three separate octagonal caps, each 18 px across, centred on its piece
flat top in palette 88 with a crisp chamfered rim (lit edge upper-left, dark lower-right from the light, not paint)
the tallest parts of the model: clearly thicker than the canisters and connectors, casting a shadow on them (sprite rows 18-19)
hard surface: flat top, straight sides, no bulging
features.note: The concept draws them as thick armoured caps sitting above the canisters.

traits: a block between each pair of caps (sprite cols 20-27 and 44-51, rows 11-19), widening downwards at rows 15-19
lit top edge at row 12 (a chamfer), body palette 89
lower than the caps, about as high as the canisters
features.note: Concept: the dark coupling block between the caps.

traits: six upright canisters side by side from the caps to the bottom edge (cols 12-19, 20-28, 28-35, 36-43, 44-52, 52-59)
each a separate hard-edged tank with chamfered long edges and a flat top, seams (dark lines) between them
the canisters at cols 28-35 and 52-59 are lighter (palette 90); the others palette 89
they run under the caps' lower edge and stand clearly above the rock bed
features.note: Concept: the row of upright canisters below the caps.

the groove is a dark recess, not painted
features.note: Sprite rows 22-25: dark band then a lit diagonal edge.

round, matte stones about half as tall as they are wide
grey boulders fill the gaps between the caps above the connectors (cols 20-27 and 44-51, rows 4-11) and the sides at both ends
